questions.question: Case Study: Frederick $W$. Smith and FedEx: In 1965, Yale University undergraduate Frederick $W$. Smith wrote a term paper about the passenger route systems used by most shippers, which he viewed as economically inadequate. Smith wrote of the need for shippers to have an innovative system designed specifically for airfreight that could accommodate time-sensitive shipments such as medicines, computer parts and electronics. His professor gave him a “$C$”. But he got an A from the marketplace when he launched Federal Express in August 1971. Today FedEx carries 2.1 million envelopes and packages every night; 1.3 million of them arrive at Tennessee alone, where swarms of planes stack up at night waiting to land. Scanners, conveyor belts, workers, delivery trucks, satellite dishes and all form a system that generated \$29.4 billion in sales in 2005 and employs 215,838 workers. Humble beginning: In August of 1971 following a stint in the military, Smith bought controlling interest in Arkansas Aviation Sales, located in Little Rock, Ark. While operating his new firm, Smith identified the tremendous difficulty in getting packages and other airfreight delivered within one to two days. This dilemma motivated him to do the necessary research for resolving the inefficient distribution system. Thus, the idea for Federal Express was born: a company that revolutionized global business practices and now defines speed and reliability. Federal Express was so-named due to the patriotic meaning associated with the word "Federal," which suggested an interest in nationwide economic activity. At that time, Smith hoped to obtain a contract with the Federal Reserve Bank and, although the proposal was denied, he believed the name was a particularly good one for attracting public attention and maintaining name recognition. The company incorporated in June 1971 and officially began operations on April 17, 1973, with the launch of 14 small aircraft from Memphis International Airport. On that night, Federal Express delivered 186 packages to 25 $U$.$S$. Page 2 of 3 cities from Rochester, NY, to Miami, Fla. In the $mid-1970s$, Federal Express took a leading role in lobbying for air cargo deregulation that finally came in 1977. These changes allowed Federal Express to use larger aircraft (such as Boeing $727s$ and McDonnell-Douglas $DC-10s)$ and spurred the company's rapid growth. Today FedEx Express has the world's largest all-cargo air fleet, including McDonnell-Douglass $MD-11s$ and Airbus $A-300s$ and $A-310s$. The planes have a total daily lift capacity of more than 26.5 million pounds. In a 24-hour period, the fleet travels nearly 500,000 miles while its couriers $\log$ 2.5 million miles a day - the equivalent of $10^{\wedge 0}$ trips around the earth. FedEx Customer Information Services was established in 2002 as a subsidiary of FedEx Corporate Services, Inc., to align customer contact centers, worldwide revenue operations, claims, $\operatorname{trace}$ and package engineering within FedEx’s professional services company. They had now established an online shipment tracking system wherein the customers could track the status of their shipments online by logging onto the FedEx website and entering the shipment number. Today, FedEx is ranked 214 in the Fortune 500 Global Companies. FedEx Supply Chain Services provides transportation and logistics management, consulting services and other customized supply chain solutions so that customers can maximize potential and minimize costs. Questions: i. As a MIS executive, what type of a Logical Database structure you think would be ideal to track shipments in this case? Justify your answer. ii. Mention any 3 advantages that the Online shipment tracking systems have over the conventional tracking system (i.e. calling the office for shipment enquiries) iii. What file organization methods support online processing, what are the advantages and limitations of the same and what is the basic distinction between these methods? iv. Why is file management important for the overall system performance of an organization? [02 + 03 + 03 + 02 = 10 Marks] Page 3 of 3
